newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: South African bond and currency markets enjoyed a strong intraday session on Tuesday, both ending on a firm note.
On the bond market, the key R150 stock was last trading at 15.900 percent -- its intraday best level -- from 16.12 percent late on Monday.
The market started the day strong, buoyed by a newspaper report that government was considering cancelling about five billion rand in spending from budget rollovers to bring down the budget deficit.

In addition, the release of a sightly better-than-expected producer price index figure for November at 8.5 percent year-on-year against an anticipated 8.7 percent and 0.5 percent month-on-month from an expected 0.7 percent aided the trend, as did the stronger rand.
Stockbrokers Huysamer Stals anticipated December PPI to rise marginally on a year-to-year basis to 8.66 percent from 8.5 percent in November, based on a month-on-month rise of 0.88 percent.

"The newspaper report that government is trying to cut spending to bring down the budget deficit, the PPI figure and the currency combined to give a strong buying signal to the market," a senior bond trader said.
He said it was possible the market had been slightly overbought and expected major resistance at around the 15.75 percent level on the downside.
Over the next few days, bond traders expected the market to hold in a 15.94 to 16.04 percent range.
They said easier money market conditions had aided the bullish trend but cautioned that liquidity was still tight.
The daily money market shortage fell to 9.499 billion rand on Monday from 10.322 billion rand on Saturday and 11.13 billion at the end of December.
Tuesday's strength had again come on the back of good foreign interest, which had also driven Monday's gains.
The market was now awaiting the release of December reserves data, due out late on Wednesday.
A Reuters consensus poll of seven economists forecast reserves would decline to 10.85 billion rand after rising to 10.93 billion rand in November from October's rise to 10.28 billion rand.
Reserve Bank intervention in the currency market and the repayment of foreign debt are expected to have brought a two-month recovery in reserves to an end in December, according to economists.
Foreigners bought 62.25 million rands worth of South African bonds on Monday, the Bond Exchange said.
Nominal cumulative turnover was 2.80 billion rand on Monday from 33.48 billion rand on Friday, Bond Exchange statistics showed.
The rand had a strong run, firming close to four cents in the early morning as players were caught long dollars overnight and offshore banks sold the U.S. unit in bond driven orders.
The currency moved to below the 4.66 level on the dollar but importer demand around that level saw it retrace.
"The market was caught long overnight and players started selling dollars once it became clear that there was not the same amount of dollar demand as on Monday," a forex trader said.
She said bond market strength had been key in driving the currency firmer.
Another forex trader expected the rand to hold below 4.70 at the opening on Wednesday but said much would depend on the level of importer dollar demand.
Against the crosses, the rand was last trading at 7.9072/9203 on sterling from 7.8992/9123 late on Monday and at 0.3340/3345 on the mark from 0.3326/3331 previously.
On the money market, three-month NCD rates moved slightly lower to between 17.35 and 17.75 percent from 17.40 and 17.75 percent while the 90-day BA rate was also lower at 16.65 and 16.95 percent.
The money market shortage fell back below the 10 billion mark on Monday to 9.499 billion rand from 10.322 billion rand on Saturday.
-- Vera von Lieres, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003
